A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AGEA research. The complete main texts and appendices A–E support comparison, including equations, algorithms, tables, and all six figures.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix E report original attack experiments measuring graph leakage and precision across Medical, Agriculture, and Novel corpora.

after.justification: The original experiments are retained, and Appendix E.1 adds hyperparameter sensitivity results on Medical with M-GraphRAG.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, the two-stage extraction pipeline, graph/query memories, novelty-guided mode selection, and exploitation targeting remain unchanged. Minor prompt wording edits preserve the same filtering instructions and operations.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same Medical, Agriculture, individual Novel graphs, and full 20-book corpus. The M-GraphRAG, LightRAG, and Naive-RAG scenarios are retained; the new sensitivity study uses existing coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding main and Naive-RAG comparisons retain IKEA, CopyBreakRAG, TGTB, and PIDE; the Novel comparison retains TGTB and PIDE. Newly discussed GRASP and AURA are not evaluated as comparators.

E3.justification: New Table 6 introduces a 250-query Medical/M-GraphRAG experiment varying initial exploration probability, decay, novelty threshold, and window size, with forced modes and failure detection disabled. Previously reported budgets, models, retrieval settings, preprocessing, and metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix E.1 adds a focused analysis of policy sensitivity and the contribution of exploration-failure detection. Existing component and command ablations, scalability analyses, Naive-RAG analysis, and response examples are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for its experimental results. The new sensitivity table continues the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: All ten earlier tables retain their numerical entries after matching renumbered tables. New Table 6 adds sensitivity results, including 38.6% node precision with k=1 versus 92.9% for the default. Appendix D.2 removes the earlier 8.32 versus 5.84 edges-per-turn comparison.

T1.justification: The threat model, equations 1–14, novelty definition including zero-count cases, and formal mode-selection rules are unchanged. Added exploration–exploitation citations introduce no new mathematical results or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and listed contributions retain the budgeted black-box reconstruction problem, the first agentic AGEA framework claim, and the claim of recovering up to 90% of nodes and edges with high precision. The central experimental conclusions remain unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 newly discusses dependence on graph construction, retrieval design, and corpus quality, while clarifying existing output-format and defense exclusions. Appendix E.1 adds interpretations of policy sensitivity, and the conclusion tentatively extends privacy implications beyond text-only GraphRAG.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-availability statement and repository pointer, identifies CloudBank computational support, and documents the new sensitivity settings. Existing implementation details, prompts, and default configurations are retained; repository contents are not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: Section 2 and Appendices A.2–A.3 substantially revise positioning through GRASP and AURA. V1 claims no prior work studies latent-graph extraction under a fixed budget; v2 acknowledges budgeted subgraph reconstruction and distinguishes automatic recovery of larger graph portions. It also expands discussion of GraphRAG defenses and graph-assisted LLM research.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites expand related work, the conclusion, and limitations, shorten ethical considerations, and add acknowledgments and Appendix E.1. Affiliation and terminology receive edits, while the overall organization and most methodological and appendix prose remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds sensitivity Table 6 and renumbers the later tables. Existing displays are relocated or reflowed, including Table 1 joining Figure 2 on PDF page 7, and Table 2's caption is shortened. All six figures retain their visual content.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful evidence about policy sensitivity, better acknowledges closely related attacks and defenses, and states applicability limits more clearly. The code-access pointer also improves documentation. These are incremental gains: the core method and previous results remain unchanged, while the new study covers one dataset/system at 250 queries without run-to-run uncertainty, and broader privacy implications remain untested.
